title: opencode-container: launcher skills passthrough subcommand
description: opencode-container skills <list|enable|disable|status|deps|gate> ... runs a one-shot container with --entrypoint python3 executing /opt/my-skills/scripts/install_skills.py (distroless-safe, no shell). Global ops mount only the state dir; project ops also mount cwd at /workspace. No interactive launcher UI.

title: opencode-container: bake my-skills into image (make skills, vendor pin, /opt paths)
description: make skills clones tslator/my-skills (private; host gh/SSH auth) at a pinned commit into vendor/my-skills/; vendor/my-skills.sha records the pin. Dockerfile final stage: COPY vendor/my-skills /opt/my-skills (root-owned) + symlink /opt/skills -> /opt/my-skills. Default config/opencode.json ships with NO skills key (content present, nothing enabled).

title: my-skills: add --config FILE global-config target to enable/disable
description: Extend install_skills.py enable/disable with a --config FILE target so the image-baked installer can merge skill paths into /app/.config/opencode/opencode.json using the existing JSONC-preserving edits. Keep all path/layout knowledge in the installer.

title: Verify OpenCode skills config assumptions (merge, watcher, unknown paths)
description: Blocking validation gate from docs/plan-skills-in-image.md. Test with two config files: (1) project-level skills array APPENDS to global skills array rather than replacing it; (2) editing skills while a session runs is picked up by the watcher or requires restart - document result; (3) unknown/missing paths in skills degrade with a warning, not a hard failure.

title: Epic: bake my-skills library into container image (skills-in-image)
description: Make tslator/my-skills skills available to in-container OpenCode without --host-access. Image = content, native skills key = state, installer = writer, agent = interviewer, launcher = thin plumbing. Full design: docs/plan-skills-in-image.md

title: Implement host bdui user service + launcher auto-registration
description: Implement the uch design (concurrency safety verified — embedded dolt handles host+container concurrent access on the same .beads; see uch CORRECTION comment). Sketch: ~/.config/systemd/user/bdui.service running node /usr/lib/node_modules/beads-ui/server/index.js (or host npm equivalent) in foreground, Type=simple, HOST=127.0.0.1 PORT=3000, BDUI_RUNTIME_DIR pinned; unit wrapper re-POSTs every entry of ~/.opencode-container/bdui-workspaces.json after server start (in-memory registrations die with the daemon; 'bdui restart' only persists via CLI re-POST). Launcher: when workspace has .beads and host bdui answers on 127.0.0.1:3000, POST /api/register-workspace {path,database} with HOST paths and append to bdui-workspaces.json; silent no-op when service absent. Decide interaction with --bdui flag (keep as container-private alternative). Update README bdui section.

title: Investigate: host-level bdui systemd service + auto-register container workspaces
description:
Goal: one host bdui instance (user systemd service, e.g. systemd --user unit running 'bdui start' on 127.0.0.1:3000) is the single viewer for ALL projects. opencode-container no longer needs to run its own bdui; instead, launching it in a workspace that has .beads/ causes that workspace to appear in the host bdui workspace dropdown automatically.

Design sketch:
- Host: user systemd service keeps bdui alive (Type=forking or wrapper; bdui start daemonizes today - investigate best unit shape, Restart policy, BDUI_RUNTIME_DIR pin).
- Registration trigger: when opencode-container starts with a workspace containing .beads/, something POSTs {path, database} to /api/register-workspace. Two candidate registrars:
  a) LAUNCHER-side (host): curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/register-workspace with the HOST path (launcher knows $WORKSPACE). Simple, no container network changes, correct host paths for free.
  b) Container-side: bootstrap POSTs via host alias (needs --host-access style add-host AND bdui must not be loopback-bound - a 127.0.0.1-bound host service is unreachable from the container netns). Only pick this if in-container registration is truly needed.
  Default assumption: (a).

Known facts (verified 2026-11-17, beads-ui 0.12.6):
- POST /api/register-workspace requires both 'path' and 'database' (absolute host paths); returns {ok:true,registered:path}. GET /api/workspaces lists them; UI has a workspace picker dropdown.
- bdui shells out to host bd, so host must have bd installed and able to open each repo's beads DB (Dolt). Investigate concurrent access: container bd + host bd reading/writing the same .beads Dolt DB simultaneously - lock behavior, corruption risk, beads sync model.
- bdui CLI surface is only start/stop/restart; no register CLI command.

Investigate / open questions:
1. Persistence: does register-workspace survive bdui restart (registry file under BDUI_RUNTIME_DIR? registry-watcher.js role)? If not, systemd ExecStartPost or a small register-on-boot scan.
2. Staleness: removed/renamed projects lingering in dropdown - does bdui prune dead workspaces? Need periodic reconcile or accept manual?
3. Dedup/idempotency of repeated registrations from repeated launches (same path twice).
4. Security: any local process can register arbitrary paths; is that acceptable on a single-user machine? bdui binds 127.0.0.1 only.
5. Interaction with existing per-container --bdui flag: keep as opt-in alternative (container-private beads DBs), add --bdui-host / auto-register path, or replace? Propose UX and update README section accordingly.
6. Deliverable: working ~/.config/systemd/user/bdui.service + launcher auto-registration (likely in bin/opencode-container when $WORKSPACE/.beads exists and host bdui responds), documented in README.

Deliverable: findings comment on this bead with recommended design (unit file contents, registration mechanism, concurrency verdict), plus follow-up implementation bead(s) if accepted.

comments.author: Tim Slator
comments.text:
FINDINGS — recommended design is BLOCKED on a beads concurrency bug; details:

(1) bdui registry model (source-verified, beads-ui 0.12.6): two sources merged per request — file-based ~/.beads/registry.json (written only by bd *daemons*; plain bd commands in embedded mode never write it — confirmed absent on host and container after heavy bd use) and in-memory API registrations. registry-watcher fs.watch exists but the change callback only logs. So the host dropdown starts empty and only fills via POST /api/register-workspace or 'bdui start' cwd-registration.

(2) Persistence: in-memory registrations survive 'bdui restart' ONLY because the CLI fetches workspaces from the old server and re-POSTs them (commands.js ~L247-277). Crash/systemctl-restart of the daemon loses them. Mitigation if pursued: launcher appends host paths to a persistent list (e.g. ~/.opencode-container/bdui-workspaces.json) and the unit's wrapper re-POSTs all entries after server start.

(3) Registration trigger: launcher-side POST from host is right (launcher knows real host paths; container-side would need non-loopback bind + host alias — unnecessary).

(4) BLOCKER — cross-namespace concurrent bd access silently loses writes. Empirical (embeddeddolt mode, rootless podman keep-id, same .beads dir):
  - host-write vs container-write: host writes 0/6 survived (container's won)
  - container-write vs host-READ loop: container writes 0/8 then 0/4 survived — creates returned rc=0 with issue IDs, then vanished
  - host-process vs host-process writes: 16/16 safe (bd's designed case)
  Sequential host↔container access is fine (reads and writes interop; keep-id makes container writes land as host uid).
  Mechanism (hypothesis): embedded dolt debounce keeps a live in-process server per bd burst; the gate lock's staleness logic misjudges cross-PID-namespace holders, so two embedded servers run split-brain against one data dir, last-flush wins. bdui inline-editing makes host bdui a WRITER, so this bites the exact proposed workflow (view+edit in host UI while container agent works the same DB).

(5) Safe paths forward (pick one before implementing):
  a) bd server mode: 'bd dolt start' runs a real dolt sql-server all bd processes connect to — designed for multi-process. Cross-namespace wrinkle: host server + container clients need non-localhost bind + host alias (or per-project servers with published ports). Needs a follow-up investigation bead.
  b) Report upstream to gastownhall/beads: cross-namespace embedded-mode lock failure = silent data loss; strong bug regardless of this feature.
  c) Keep x93 per-container bdui (DB touched by exactly one namespace at a time) — current shipped design, safe.

RECOMMENDATION: keep per-container --bdui as default; file (a) investigation + (b) upstream report; revisit host-bdui service only after server-mode path proves out. Follow-up beads created.

comments.author: Tim Slator
comments.text: CORRECTION — retract the (4) BLOCKER and (5) analysis: the lost-write tests were invalid. The host-side loops ran in the wrapper shell whose cwd was the opencode-container repo (the 'cd' was swallowed into the backgrounded '&&' chain), so 'lost' host writes actually landed in the opencode-container beads DB (visible as stray host-loop-*/race-host-* issues, since deleted), and 'lost' container writes were an artifact of listing the wrong DB. Redone with explicit per-command cwd: host-write vs container-write concurrent = 6/6 + 6/6 survived; container-write vs host-read-loop = 8/8 survived. CONCLUSION: host bd + container bd on the same .beads via bind mount (rootless keep-id) is SAFE for concurrent use; embedded dolt locking works across PID namespaces. The proposed host-bdui architecture is VIABLE. Valid findings stand: (1) dropdown fills only via POST /api/register-workspace or bdui-start cwd registration (file registry unused by embedded-mode bd); (2) registrations survive 'bdui restart' only via CLI re-POST, not daemon crash — persist a list and re-register in the unit; (3) launcher-side POST is the right trigger. ufq/rnu/b1h follow-ups deleted as moot; 2ef unblocked and is the implementation bead.

title: Isolate /app/.opencode/plan per workspace
description: Plan-mode files are written to /app/.opencode/plan, which lives on the shared ~/.opencode-container home mount, so plan files from one workspace are visible in another. Mount a per-workspace dir (e.g. projects/<name>-<hash>/plan) at /app/.opencode/plan the same way share/state are isolated. Note: /app/.opencode may also hold user custom commands/themes, so mount only the plan subdir.

comments.author: Tim Slator
comments.text: PATH CORRECTION: on opencode 2.2.6 the plan-mode default is NOT /app/.opencode/plan. Binary strings show config key plansDirectory: 'Custom directory for plan files, relative to project root. If not set, defaults to ~/.clau[de]/plans/' - i.e. plans land in $HOME/.claude/plans (Claude Code compat), which on the shared /app home mount leaked across workspaces exactly as described. Fix implemented at the corrected path: launcher creates $ws_root/plans and mounts it at /app/.claude/plans (same per-workspace pattern as share/state). plansDirectory was rejected as an approach: it is project-root-relative, so it would write plans into the user's repo. Verified: test_launcher.sh asserts the new mount; live engine run with the same mount pair wrote /app/.claude/plans/plan-a.md and host saw it in the backing dir (engine auto-creates the missing .claude parent under the /app bind mount). Host files land under ~/.opencode-container/projects/<name>-<hash>/plans/, owned by the container app uid via rootless subuid mapping - same as existing share/state behavior.

title: Add bdui (beads-ui) to image and explore terminal viewing options
description:
Add the beads-ui npm package (bdui CLI) to the container image, and investigate ways to view the bdui web UI from a terminal.

Context:
- bdui = npm package beads-ui (https://github.com/mantoni/beads-ui), Express + lit-html SPA + WebSocket, default 127.0.0.1:3000.
- Image already ships Node 24 and bd; beads-ui shells out to bd, so runtime deps are Node-only (no new shared libs for collect-runtime-deps.sh).

Part 1 — add to image:
- Install beads-ui pinned (npm install -g beads-ui@<ver>) in builder-tools or agent-tools stage; verify bdui --version.
- Launcher (bin/opencode-container): add option to publish/expose port 3000 (e.g. -p 3000:3000 or --publish) and optionally run bdui start --host 0.0.0.0 inside the container.
- Update AGENTS.md/README tool list.

Part 2 — terminal viewing options to explore:
1. Text browsers (lynx/w3m/elinks): NO-JS, SPA renders blank — likely dead end, confirm quickly.
2. Headless render pipeline: chromium --headless --dump-dom | pandoc/readability -> glow; heavy, distroless-hostile.
3. Drive bdui's REST/WS API from terminal with curl+jq or an fzf TUI (bd CLI already covers most of this).
4. Practical fallback: port-publish + host browser (not terminal, but simplest working path).
5. Check if bdui has any static/SSR or export mode usable by text browsers.

Deliverable: bead 1 implemented (or documented why not), findings comment on terminal options with a recommendation.
notes:
DECISION: go with option 1 — port-publish + host browser. No text browsers, no headless render pipeline.

Multi-project considerations (N project folders = N concurrent bdui needs):
- PID/runtime conflict: bdui daemonizes with server.pid in BDUI_RUNTIME_DIR (default $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/beads-ui). Two projects on one host collide — second bdui start attaches to/fights the first server. Current workaround: BDUI_RUNTIME_DIR="\$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/bdui-\$(basename \$PWD)" + port 3000+cksum(PWD)%1000.
- Running bdui INSIDE each container sidesteps this: each container has its own runtime dir + netns; only the host-published port must be unique.
- Launcher needs deterministic host-port allocation, e.g. -p 127.0.0.1:\$((3000+cksum(pwd)%1000)):3000. Caveats: cksum%1000 birthday collisions (~38 projects for 50% chance), and port may already be in use on host. Alternatives: -p 127.0.0.1::3000 (random) + docker port query, or --bdui-port flag override.
- ALTERNATIVE worth evaluating first: bdui natively supports multiple workspaces (POST /api/register-workspace, GET /api/workspaces, UI workspace picker, registry-watcher.js). One host-level bdui instance could register every project folder (host bd reads each repo's beads DB directly) → single port, in-UI project switching, zero per-project port/runtime-dir juggling. Per-container bdui then only needed if the beads DB must stay container-private.

Acceptance:
- bdui pinned+installed in image; bdui --version works in container.
- Launcher flag (e.g. --bdui) starts bdui --host 0.0.0.0 in-container and publishes a per-project unique 127.0.0.1 host port; prints exact URL.
- Document multi-project behavior + the single-host-bdui alternative in README/AGENTS.md.

comments.author: Tim Slator
comments.text: FINDINGS (terminal viewing options): option 2 (headless chromium render pipeline) rejected — heavy, distroless-hostile, no chromium in base and no exec into prod container. Option 3 (curl+jq/fzf over bdui REST) redundant — bd CLI already covers terminal querying; bdui API adds no terminal-only capability. Option 5: bdui has no static/SSR/export mode (CLI surface is only start/stop/restart; SPA needs JS), so text browsers (option 1-as-browsers) are out. Shipped option 4-as-primary per DECISION note: --bdui flag -> bootstrap runs 'bdui start --host 0.0.0.0' in-container (auto-registers /workspace/.beads from cwd), launcher publishes 127.0.0.1 host port = 3000 + cksum(workspace)%1000 (--bdui-port override, OPENCODE_CONTAINER_BDUI[_PORT] env opt-ins), prints exact URL. Per-container isolation is automatic: own netns + BDUI_RUNTIME_DIR defaults to /tmp per container. Verified live: launcher printed http://127.0.0.1:3289/, host curl got workspace JSON + SPA 200, teardown released port. Single-host alternative documented in README: host bdui + POST /api/register-workspace {path,database} (verified 200); prefer when beads DBs need not stay container-private. Collision caveat documented: hash collisions possible in 1000-port space, override flag exists.
